history.summary: Trikuta temple complex at Keladi village, ~8 km from Sagara on the Sagara-Soraba road (CSV town 'Shimoga' corrected: the temple is at Keladi, not Shimoga city). Commissioned by Chowdappa (Chavuda) Nayaka c. 1500 CE, when Keladi was the first Nayaka capital before the shift to Ikkeri. Three shrines: Rameshwara (central), Veerabhadra, and Parvati, with Rameshwara and Veerabhadra sharing a common mukhamandapa. Built of greenish-grey schist in mixed Hoysala-Dravida style with Kadamba influence; noted for the Gandabherunda (double-headed bird) ceiling carving in the Veerabhadra shrine, yali/Vali pillars, intricate red-sandalwood carving in the Parvati shrine, and a Nandi dwajastambha erected under Rani Chennamma. Legend: the linga was found in an ant-hill over which Chowdappa's cow shed milk daily. A museum of Keladi-dynasty manuscripts and artefacts stands nearby. Maintained by the ASI/state archaeology.

name: Rameshwara Temple, Keladi
town_description: Keladi is a small village in Sagara taluk of Shivamogga district, about 8 km from Sagara town on the Sagara-Soraba road. It was the first capital of the Keladi (Ikkeri) Nayakas before the capital was shifted to Ikkeri in the early-to-mid 16th century. The village is dominated by the historic Rameshwara temple complex and a museum housing manuscripts and artefacts of the Nayaka period, making it a quiet but significant heritage destination in the Malnad.
